mainEntity.name: How much does a Land Rover Defender 130 TD5 engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full reconditioned or rebuilt Land Rover Defender 130 TD5 engine typically costs between £2,200 and £5,000 for the unit itself, depending on whether it is a 10P or 15P code and the level of rebuild.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of injector loom failure in a Land Rover Defender 130 TD5?

acceptedAnswer.text: Early detection is critical to preventing catastrophic ECU damage in your TD5 engine. Look for rough idling, misfires, or the engine cutting out unexpectedly. A telltale sign is oil residue around the ECU connector or a burning electrical smell from the engine bay.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a classic Land Rover Defender 130 TD5?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, especially given the rising collector and utility values of well-maintained long-wheelbase Defenders. A rebuilt TD5 engine with upgraded steel dowels and a revised loom can extend the vehicle's life by decades.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the TD5 10P and 15P engine codes in the Defender 130?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both are 2.5-litre, 122hp 5-cylinder diesel engines, but the 15P (introduced in 2002) is a significantly revised and more reliable version. The 15P features steel cylinder head locating dowels and an updated, sealed injector loom to prevent oil contamination.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Land Rover Defender 130 TD5 engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A straightforward supply and fit of a reconditioned TD5 engine typically takes 2 to 3 days at a specialist workshop. This allows time for proper bedding-in procedures, fluid checks, and a thorough road test.

historyTimeline.h2: Land Rover Defender 130 TD5 - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: When the TD5 engine was introduced to the Defender 130 lineup, it brought electronic fuel injection and improved refinement to Land Rover's iconic long-wheelbase workhorse, replacing the earlier 300Tdi unit. Over its production run, the TD5 saw critical reliability updates to address early teething issues.

milestones.description: TD5 10P, 2.5L, 122hp (Introduction of the electronically controlled 5-cylinder diesel to the Defender 130, replacing the 300Tdi)
TD5 15P, 2.5L, 122hp (Major reliability update: revised ECU, steel head locating dowels, and updated injector loom to prevent oil contamination)
Production of the TD5 Defender 130 ends, replaced by the Ford-sourced 2.4 TDCi (Puma) engine.

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Land Rover Defender 130 TD5 is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

problems.group: Injector Loom Oil Leak & ECU Contamination
problems.h4: Injector Loom Oil Leak & ECU Contamination - Why the Land Rover Defender 130 TD5 10P Fails
problems.rootCause: The factory injector harness loom degrades over time, allowing engine oil to wick along the wires and pool inside the Engine Control Unit (ECU), causing catastrophic electrical failure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Fit an updated, sealed injector loom and clean the ECU connector.
repairOptions.longevity: Highly recommended for all 10P models to prevent total ECU failure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: The right call if the ECU is destroyed and the engine has high mileage or other compounding issues.

problems.recommendation: If your Defender 130 TD5 is a 10P model, a preventative injector loom replacement is a mandatory, low-cost fix that can save your ECU. If the engine has already suffered catastrophic head gasket failure with no bottom-end damage, a specialist top-end rebuild with steel dowels is cost-effective. However, if the engine has high mileage, oil consumption, or a history of overheating, a full reconditioned replacement is the most reliable long-term investment.

problems.h4: Head Gasket Failure - Why the Land Rover Defender 130 TD5 Wears Prematurely
problems.rootCause: Early 10P models used plastic cylinder head locating dowels that could shear under thermal stress, compromising the head gasket seal. The 15P updated this to steel dowels.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Strip top end, machine head, fit upgraded steel-dowel head gasket kit.
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if the block and crankshaft are undamaged and compression is good.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: The right call if there is bottom-end wear, a cracked head, or you want long-term reliability for a keeper vehicle.
